messages:
olivia (support): seeing a burst of 502s hitting hosted-api eu1 right after the auth rotation at ~09:58 UTC. customer reports: generation requests returning 502 or long tail 504s. can we triage?
ajay (eng-sre): can you drop a sample trace id and a small repro? also are these streaming or short requests?
olivia (support): mainly streaming embed/generate calls from a few customers. sample trace ids: trace=trc_7a1b2c, trc_9f8e76. curl repro i used (short):
```
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"embed-small","input":"hello world","stream":true}' \
  "https://eu1-api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings"
```
maria (support): customer A attached logs showing 502s started ~60s after their token rotated and their client retried aggressively. they saw 15% failure rate for ~5 minutes.
lina (platform): infra telemetry shows auth-service deploy-bot rolled v2.1.3 -> v2.2.0 at 09:58:40 UTC. deploy-bot: deploy succeeded.
deploy-bot: "auth-service v2.2.0 deployed to eu1 at 2026-03-17T09:58:40Z" :white_check_mark:
ajay (eng-sre): pulled envoy upstream logs, snippet: 
```
[2026-03-17T09:59:05.123Z] envoy upstream reset: upstream_reset_reason=connection_failure, code=0x1
[2026-03-17T09:59:05.124Z] upstream request reset: connection close, downstream_stream_id=1242
```
sam (oncall): tcpdump around that window shows a flurry of FIN/RESET from clients when auth responses took >500ms. keepalive pools per frontdoor worker look saturated during the spike.
ajay (eng-sre): hypothesis: token rotation caused short auth backend stalls -> a subset of client connections retried -> frontdoor worker connection windows (h2 keepalive slots) got pinned by long-lived streaming sessions -> new upstream handshakes failed, envoy returned 502. also saw 504s when heavy backpressure delayed response.
olivia (support): reproduced locally by rotating tokens and firing concurrent 120 streaming embed requests (clients keepalive 75s). got ~12% 502 at peak. repro steps: increase concurrent streams gradually, rotate token, observe 502s after first few reconnections.
lina (platform): config checks: frontdoor envoy keepalive_max_streams=64, per-worker conn_window=128. with streams pinned and auth bursts we can exceed half the pool.
ajay (eng-sre): quick mitigation options: 1) short-term: increase per-worker conn window and buff limits on eu1 frontline (will require restart) 2) add auth-service auto-retry/backoff to smooth token rotation bursts 3) add temporary rate-limit on client reconnects for streaming endpoints. I can do (1) as a fast rollback knob, but need approvers.
maria (support): customers asking for ETA. can we communicate workaround: ask clients to backoff jitter on token refresh?
olivia (support): yes ask customers to stagger token refreshes and add jitter; i'll patch customer-facing note.
ajay (eng-sre): action items: - ajay will bump frontdoor keepalive slots to 192 on eu1 (hot config) and watch for regression (10m window) - lina to open a follow-up to throttle auth rotation bursts and add circuit-breaker on auth cache misses - sam to collect pcap and envoy traces and attach to incident ticket - olivia/maria to send interim customer note advising jittered refresh and exponential backoff.
lina (platform): created ticket INF-4921: "auth-rotation -> connwindow exhaustion -> 502/504 mitigation and long-term fix" with initial notes.
infra-bot: scheduled job: bumping frontdoor worker conn limit on eu1 at 10:12 UTC (dry-run).
ajay (eng-sre): after bump applied, 502 rate dropped from ~12% to <1% within 180s. keeping monitoring for 30m.
olivia (support): customers confirm improvement, still watching for residual latency spikes. thanks team :pray: 
maria (support): putting postmortem draft on incidents/ when stable. will include repro steps and recommended client-side jitter sample code.
ajay (eng-sre): provisional root cause: auth rotation produced synchronous cache heavy path and transient latency, concurrent long-lived streaming connections pinned keepalive resources causing envoy upstream handshake failures -> 502. long-term fixes: auth async refresh, connection pool backpressure, client reconnect jitter.
olivia (support): adding short client example for jittered refresh: 
```
function refreshTokenWithJitter() {
  const jitter = Math.random() * 2000; // 0-2s
  setTimeout(refreshToken, 30000 + jitter);
}
```
sam (oncall): attaching traces and pcap to INF-4921. will follow up if we see recurrence.
olivia (support): closing thread for now, reopen if any new 502 cluster seen. :lock:"
